verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents its own failure alerting through email, Slack and webhooks, and a real-time trace view with logs in its dashboard. There is no evidence that failure rates, latencies or queue depths can be exported to an external observability stack. Alerting is documented only for task failures, not broader misbehavior. Missing for 10: metrics export to external observability tools (e.g., OpenTelemetry/Prometheus/Datadog), documented failure-rate/latency/queue-depth metrics, alerts on conditions beyond task failure, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, failure rates, latencies, and queue depths export to my observability stack, and alerts fire when workflows misbehave

citations.quote: Receive alerts via email, Slack notification and webhooks when your tasks fail.
the run page will show a trace view of each task executing in real-time along with any logs it produces.
